title: Coherence and ideal annihilation of a tensor multiplication kernel
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], I a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], H a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and n a nonnegative integer. Put T=I^n \otimes H [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and let mu:T \to H be multiplication. Then T is coherent, ker(mu) is quasi-coherent, and I^n ker(mu)=0, with the recursive ideal power and multiplication-image product [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk].

source.place: Tag 01YB, second Artin-Rees argument and last displayed map

proof.text: Put J=I^n as IdealSheafData and T=J.toModules tensor H. Coherence makes H quasi-coherent by the locally Noetherian coherence criterion. The private ideal-qc helper realizes J.toModules as the kernel of the structure-sheaf map to the closed-subscheme pushforward; qcqs pushforward preserves quasi-coherence, and the quasi-coherent kernel theorem gives quasi-coherence of J.toModules. The affine tensor theorem gives quasi-coherence of T and surjectivity of its tensor section comparison.

On an affine U, the section ring is Noetherian. Compose the section inclusion of J with unitSectionsEquiv.symm to get an injective linear map into that ring. Module.Finite.of_injective makes the sections of J finite, and coherent_affine_sections_finite makes the sections of H finite. Mathlib Module.Finite.tensorProduct and Module.Finite.of_surjective applied to tensorSectionsMap make the sections of T finite. Apply the affine-cover finite-type criterion on all affine opens, then the locally Noetherian coherence criterion to obtain coherence of T.

The existing quasi-coherent kernel theorem applied to the multiplication map mu:T to H gives quasi-coherence of K=kernel(mu). This uses only quasi-coherence, without requiring coherent-kernel closure.

For sections a,b of J and h of H on any open U, injectivity of the ideal inclusion and commutativity in O_X(U) give i(a) b=i(b) a. Bilinearity of tmulSection therefore gives i(a) times (b tensor h)=a tensor (i(b) h). Multiplication on pure tensors is mu(b tensor h)=i(b) h. These are the private helper ideal_tensor_balancing and the local equation hmu in the Lean proof.

Fix an affine U and r in I(U)^n. Since (I^n).ideal U=I.ideal U ^ n, range_toModulesι_app supplies a section a of J with i(a)=r. Let L_a:H(U) to T(U) be h mapped to a tensor h. Tensor induction and balancing give r z=L_a(mu(z)) for all sections z of T, using surjectivity of the affine tensor comparison. For k in K(U), the kernel condition gives mu(kappa(k))=0, and linearity and injectivity of kappa imply r k=0. The private multiplication-range helper identifies the product inclusion range with the multiplication range via Abelian.imageIsoImage and the affine image theorem, then computes that range by tensor induction as range(i) times the full module. Induction on recursive powers gives quasi-coherence and inclusion range I(U)^n. Therefore multiplication from the recursive power tensor K is zero on pure tensors and hence on all affine sections. Sheaf separatedness on the affine basis makes this map globally zero. Its image inclusion is zero by cancellation of the epimorphic factorThruImage, and a zero monomorphism has zero source. This proves the stated zero product, including n=0, zero and unit ideals, zero modules and the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem ideal_tensor_multiplication_kernel_control
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X]
    (I : X.IdealSheafData) (H : X.Modules)
    (hH : RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace H) (n : ℕ) :
    letI : MonoidalCategory X.Modules := SheafOfModules.monoidalCategory X.sheaf
    let T := (I ^ n).toModules ⊗ H
    let μ := (I ^ n).toModulesι ▷ H ≫ (λ_ H).hom
    RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace T ∧
      (kernel μ).IsQuasicoherent ∧
      IsZero (idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2 (kernel μ))
